section_summary: This section covers diplomatic correspondence and administrative documentation from September 1936 to December 1937 primarily concerning reciprocal income tax exemptions granted to Japanese government officials stationed in or visiting the United States under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936. Extensive lists of personnel from the Imperial Japanese Navy's Naval Inspector's Office and the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York City, as well as officials from the Department of Agriculture and Forestry, the Bureau of Monopoly, and the Department of Education, were submitted by the Japanese Embassy and processed between the State Department and the Treasury Department. Additionally, the section includes a legal inquiry concerning an automobile accident involving a former Japanese railway official, a consular report from Kobe regarding local tax compliance and the contrasting non-compliance of other foreign consulates, and a formal notification and internal legal assessment regarding a San Francisco advertising agency broadcasting radio programs on behalf of the Japanese Association of San Francisco under the Espionage Act of 1917.

subfiles.about: Internal State Department routing note regarding an inquiry on the whereabouts of Shigeru Fujii.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State (W.T.T.)
subfiles.summary: A brief internal Department of State routing and memorandum note querying whether Shigeru Fujii, referenced in a Japanese Embassy note of December 3, 1934, is the same individual inquired after by private counsel. It suggests checking with the Japanese Embassy, railway offices, or telephone directories to locate his whereabouts.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum regarding Shigeru Fujii

subfiles.about: Inquiry by law firm regarding the whereabouts and official government status of Shigeru Fujii following an automobile accident in Seattle.
subfiles.summary: The law firm Karr and Gregory, representing the Sun Indemnity Company of New York, inquires about the whereabouts and official status of Shigeru Fujii. Fujii's car was involved in an accident in Seattle on September 2, 1935, resulting in a lawsuit, and counsel received information indicating Fujii might be an agent of the Japanese Government who is returning to Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Karr and Gregory to the Department of State regarding Shigeru Fujii

subfiles.about: Department of State reply to Payne Karr regarding Shigeru Fujii's past official station in New York.
subfiles.from: Department of State (for the Secretary of State, J. C. Holmes)
subfiles.summary: The Department of State acknowledges Payne Karr's inquiry and informs him that departmental records show a Mr. Shigeru Fujii was an official of the Japanese Department of Railways stationed in New York City in 1934. The Department notes it has no further information and suggests contacting the railway office or the Japanese Consulate General in New York City.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Department of State to Payne Karr

subfiles.about: Japanese Embassy request for tax exemption for two assistant engineers of the Department of Agriculture and Forestry.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy requests that Harukazu Yabuuchi and Kodo Takamune, Assistant Engineers of the Department of Agriculture and Forestry, be added to the list of officials exempted from taxation on salaries. It notes that Yabuuchi is leaving Los Angeles on October 10, 1936, and Takamune is leaving Seattle on September 28, 1936, requesting expedited notice to local authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 205 requesting tax exemption for Harukazu Yabuuchi and Kodo Takamune

subfiles.about: State Department acknowledgment of Japanese Embassy Note No. 205.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 205 concerning tax exemptions for Harukazu Yabuuchi and Kodo Takamune. The Ambassador is informed that the request has been submitted to the appropriate United States authority with a view toward favorable action.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Yabuuchi and Takamune

subfiles.about: Secretary of State certification of reciprocity to Treasury for Harukazu Yabuuchi and Kodo Takamune.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese Note No. 205 to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr., certifying that Japan grants equivalent income tax exemptions to U.S. government employees in Japan under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936. Hull requests tax exemption for Harukazu Yabuuchi and Kodo Takamune and asks for prompt notification to collectors at Los Angeles and Seattle due to their imminent departure dates.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Treasury Department confirmation of income tax exemption for Harukazu Yabuuchi and Kodo Takamune.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (Wayne C. Taylor)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Wayne C. Taylor confirms that, in view of the State Department's certification, Harukazu Yabuuchi and Kodo Takamune are exempt from Federal income tax on their official compensation. The letter notes that the collector at Los Angeles was advised regarding Yabuuchi, while instructions arrived too late for Takamune's departure from Seattle, though no tax was apparently demanded.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury Wayne C. Taylor to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Department of State notification to the Japanese Ambassador confirming tax exemption for Yabuuchi and Takamune.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits an excerpt from the Treasury Department's letter of October 14, 1936, to the Japanese Ambassador. The communication officially informs the Ambassador that Harukazu Yabuuchi and Kodo Takamune have been held exempt from Federal income taxation on their official salaries.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador transmitting Treasury decision on Yabuuchi and Takamune

subfiles.about: Japanese Embassy confirmation of the effective date of tax exemption in Japan for American officials.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador refers to the Secretary of State's note of July 22, 1936, and previous Embassy Note No. 55 of March 21, 1936. The note clarifies that the tax exemption granted in Japan to American officials was made effective on and after January 1, 1936.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 255 regarding effective date of tax exemption in Japan

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of State letter to Treasury requesting tax refunds for three Japanese officials.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State (R. Walton Moore)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State R. Walton Moore writes to Treasury Secretary Henry Morgenthau, Jr., transmitting Japanese Embassy Notes Nos. 149 and 264 requesting refunds of income taxes paid by three Japanese officials. Moore certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936 dating back to October 14, 1932, noting that Japan never levied taxes on American officials during the period when Japanese officials were taxed in the U.S.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State R. Walton Moore to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: State Department acknowledgment of Japanese Embassy Note No. 264 regarding tax refunds.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 264 of November 27, 1936, concerning the requested refund of income taxes paid by three Japanese officials. The Ambassador is advised that the matter has been submitted to the Federal authorities and further word will follow.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding tax refund requests

subfiles.about: Japanese Embassy request for tax exemption for agricultural agronomist Shinjiro Akimoto.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption on the salary received by Shinjiro Akimoto, Agronomist of the Imperial Japanese Agricultural Experiment Station of the Department of Agriculture and Forestry, staying in New York. The note mentions that Mr. Akimoto is scheduled to sail from New York for Europe on November 25, 1936.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 254 requesting tax exemption for Shinjiro Akimoto

subfiles.about: State Department acknowledgment of Japanese Note No. 254 regarding Shinjiro Akimoto.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Note No. 254 of November 12, 1936, requesting tax exemption for Shinjiro Akimoto. The Ambassador is informed that the request has been forwarded to the appropriate authorities for action prior to Akimoto's departure on November 25.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Shinjiro Akimoto

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of State certification of reciprocity to Treasury for Shinjiro Akimoto.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State (R. Walton Moore)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State R. Walton Moore transmits Japanese Note No. 254 to Secretary of the Treasury Morgenthau, certifying reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936 for Shinjiro Akimoto. Moore requests that Akimoto's official compensation be exempted from income tax and that local officers be notified before his departure on November 25.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State R. Walton Moore to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: Japanese Embassy statement confirming non-taxation of American officials in Japan and disclaiming retroactive taxes.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador replies to the Secretary of State's note of July 22, 1936, explaining that while exemption in Japan was technically effective January 1, 1936, Japan never levied taxes on American officials residing there during the period Japanese officials were taxed in the U.S. Furthermore, Japan has no intention of levying taxes retroactively on American officials.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 264 regarding retroactive tax exemption

subfiles.about: Treasury Department confirmation of tax exemption for Shinjiro Akimoto.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (Wayne C. Taylor)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Wayne C. Taylor informs Secretary of State Hull that, pursuant to Moore's certification, Shinjiro Akimoto is held exempt from Federal income tax on his official compensation. The appropriate collector of internal revenue in New York City has been advised accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury Wayne C. Taylor to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Department of State notification to the Japanese Ambassador confirming tax exemption for Shinjiro Akimoto.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that the Treasury Department has determined Shinjiro Akimoto to be exempt from Federal income tax on his official Japanese salary. The note confirms that the internal revenue collector in New York City was notified.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Shinjiro Akimoto

subfiles.about: Treasury Department decision approving tax refunds for Hisao Okabayashi, Takeshi Takei, and Katsuji Tanaka.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (Stephen B. Gibbons)
subfiles.summary: Assistant and Acting Secretary of the Treasury Stephen B. Gibbons responds to Moore's letter of December 5, 1936, regarding refund claims. Treasury holds that Hisao Okabayashi, Takeshi Takei, and Katsuji Tanaka are exempt from Federal income tax and that local collectors will be instructed to request them to file claims for refund.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury Stephen B. Gibbons to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Department of State notification to the Japanese Ambassador regarding tax refunds for Okabayashi, Takei, and Tanaka.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State notifies the Japanese Ambassador of the Treasury Department's finding that Hisao Okabayashi, Takeshi Takei, and Katsuji Tanaka are exempt from Federal income tax. Collectors of internal revenue have been advised and instructed to request that the three officials submit formal claims for refund of taxes paid.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding refund claims for Okabayashi, Takei, and Tanaka

subfiles.about: Japanese Embassy submission of a list of 15 officials of the Naval Inspector's Office in New York requesting tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador transmits Note No. 75 and an attached roster of 15 naval officers, engineers, and clerks attached to the Naval Inspector's Office of the Imperial Japanese Navy Department in New York. Exemption from salary income taxation is requested, with the Ambassador certifying that all listed individuals are Japanese nationals and not U.S. citizens whose duties involve inspecting purchased ordnance and materials.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 75 transmitting list of Naval Inspector's Office personnel

subfiles.about: Secretary of State certification of reciprocity to Treasury for 15 personnel of the Naval Inspector's Office.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese Note No. 75 and the roster of 15 Naval Inspector's Office officials to Treasury Secretary Morgenthau. Hull certifies reciprocal exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936 and requests that the Treasury grant the tax exemption and notify the relevant revenue collectors.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: State Department transmittal to the Secretary of the Navy of the roster of Japanese Naval Inspector's Office personnel.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the Secretary of the Navy a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 75 and its roster of naval personnel attached to the Naval Inspector's Office in New York. This communication complies with the Navy Department's request of July 5, 1935, to be apprised of foreign government agents and non-diplomatic representatives residing in the United States.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: State Department acknowledgment of Japanese Note No. 75 concerning Naval Inspector's Office personnel.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 75 of March 30, 1937, enclosing the list of Naval Inspector's Office personnel in New York seeking tax exemption. The Ambassador is advised that the request has been submitted to the appropriate Federal authority.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Naval Inspector's Office list

subfiles.about: Japanese Embassy request to add Captain Misao Wada and Commander Takuji Katahira to the Naval Inspector's Office tax exemption list.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador refers to Note No. 75 and requests that Captain Misao Wada and Engineering Commander Takuji Katahira be added to the list of personnel of the Naval Inspector's Office in New York seeking salary tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 85 regarding Captain Misao Wada and Commander Takuji Katahira

subfiles.about: Secretary of State certification of reciprocity to Treasury for Captain Misao Wada and Commander Takuji Katahira.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese Note No. 85 to Treasury Secretary Morgenthau, certifying reciprocal exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936 for Captain Misao Wada and Engineering Commander Takuji Katahira. Hull requests that the two naval officers be granted exemption from income taxation on their official compensation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: State Department acknowledgment of Japanese Note No. 85 regarding Wada and Katahira.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 85 of April 10, 1937, requesting the addition of Captain Misao Wada and Engineering Commander Takuji Katahira to the tax exemption roster. The Ambassador is informed that the matter has been referred to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Wada and Katahira

subfiles.about: Japanese Embassy request for refund of income tax and bond payments required of Kozo Taniguchi and Ryokichi Sagane upon departure.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito requests the return of a $13.75 bond deposited by Kozo Taniguchi (engineer, Government-General of Taiwan) and a $20.67 cash tax payment made by Ryokichi Sagane (official, Department of Education, Tokyo) to the Internal Revenue Office in New York upon their departures for Europe. Saito stresses that both are Japanese subjects receiving compensation solely for official government duties and should be exempt.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 88 requesting tax and bond refunds for Taniguchi and Sagane

subfiles.about: Department of State request to the Japanese Embassy for job descriptions for Taniguchi and Sagane to establish reciprocity.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Note No. 88 regarding Kozo Taniguchi and Ryokichi Sagane. Citing the statutory requirement under the Act of August 27, 1935, to certify that foreign officials perform duties similar to those of American officials abroad, the Secretary requests a brief description of the specific duties performed by Messrs. Taniguchi and Sagane while in the United States.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Taniguchi and Sagane

subfiles.about: Treasury Department confirmation of income tax exemption for 15 officials of the Naval Inspector's Office.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (Roswell Magill)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill informs Secretary of State Hull that, based on State Department certification, the 15 officials of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City are held exempt from Federal income taxation on their official compensation. The collector of internal revenue in New York City will be advised accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Department of State notification to the Japanese Ambassador confirming tax exemption for 15 naval inspector officials.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that the Treasury Department has approved income tax exemption for the 15 officials attached to the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding the Naval Inspector's Office roster

subfiles.about: Treasury Department confirmation of tax exemption for Captain Misao Wada and Commander Takuji Katahira.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (Roswell Magill)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill advises Secretary of State Hull that Captain Misao Wada and Engineering Commander Takuji Katahira are exempt from Federal income tax on compensation received from the Japanese Government for official services in the United States. The New York internal revenue collector will be instructed accordingly.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Department of State notification to the Japanese Ambassador confirming tax exemption for Wada and Katahira.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State notifies the Japanese Ambassador that the Treasury Department has granted income tax exemption to Captain Misao Wada and Engineering Commander Takuji Katahira of the Naval Inspector's Office in New York, and that the local collector has been notified.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Wada and Katahira

subfiles.about: Consular report on reporting of staff incomes to Japanese tax authorities and non-compliance by other foreign consulates.
subfiles.from: American Consul, Kobe, Japan (Winthrop R. Scott)
subfiles.summary: American Consul Winthrop R. Scott in Kobe reports that the consulate complied with departmental instructions of June 13, 1936, by providing names, titles, and tax-exempt incomes of non-diplomatic staff to the Kobe Internal Revenue Office. However, Scott notes that his British, German, and French colleagues completely ignored all Japanese requests for income information on their staffs and refused to supply any data, suggesting this information may assist future discussions with the Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 113 from American Consul Winthrop R. Scott to the Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Japanese Embassy submission of a list of 11 officials of the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York requesting tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador transmits Note No. 133 and an attached list of 11 officials attached to the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York requesting income tax exemption on their official compensation. The note specifies that all listed personnel are Japanese nationals whose principal duty is inspecting railway materials purchased by the government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 133 transmitting list of Railway Office personnel

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary of State certification of reciprocity to Treasury for 11 railway officials.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles transmits Japanese Note No. 133 to Treasury Secretary Morgenthau, certifying reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936. Welles requests that the 11 Japanese railway officials stationed in New York be granted exemption from income taxation on their official compensation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State Sumner Welles to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: State Department acknowledgment of Japanese Note No. 133 concerning railway officials.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 133 of June 17, 1937, enclosing the roster of 11 railway officials in New York seeking tax exemption, stating the matter has been referred to the appropriate authorities.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Railway Office personnel

subfiles.about: Treasury Department confirmation of income tax exemption for 11 railway officials.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (Roswell Magill)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill informs the Secretary of State that, in view of Welles's certification, the 11 officials attached to the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York are exempt from Federal income tax on their official salaries, and internal revenue officers are being advised.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Department of State notification to the Japanese Ambassador confirming tax exemption for 11 railway officials.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State notifies the Japanese Ambassador that the Treasury Department has determined the 11 officials attached to the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York to be exempt from Federal income tax on their official compensation.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Railway Office personnel

subfiles.about: Notification by an advertising agency regarding radio and print advertising placed for the Japanese Association of San Francisco under the Espionage Act.
subfiles.summary: W. A. Brewer, Secretary-Treasurer of the Brewer-Weeks Company advertising agency in San Francisco, notifies the Secretary of State pursuant to the Act of June 15, 1917 (Espionage Act) that his agency was commissioned by the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Japanese Association of San Francisco to place radio talks and newspaper advertisements. While expressing a good-faith belief that the funds are private contributions from local resident Japanese members and not from the Japanese Government, the agency submits formal notification in the event that funds originated with the government.
subfiles.title: Letter from Brewer-Weeks Company to the Secretary of State regarding advertising for the Japanese Association of San Francisco

subfiles.about: State Department acknowledgment of Brewer-Weeks Company notification.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Assistant Secretary Francis B. Sayre)
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State Francis B. Sayre acknowledges receipt of W. A. Brewer's letter of October 29, 1937, stating that the agency's explanation of its relationship to the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Japanese Association of San Francisco has been noted.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary of State Francis B. Sayre to W. A. Brewer

subfiles.about: Legal Adviser's memorandum analyzing foreign agent notification and propaganda activities by Brewer-Weeks Company.
subfiles.from: Assistant Legal Adviser Richard W. Flournoy
subfiles.summary: Assistant Legal Adviser Richard W. Flournoy submits a memorandum to Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth analyzing the notification submitted by Brewer-Weeks Company under Section 3, Title VIII of the Espionage Act of June 15, 1917. Flournoy notes that while the agency's radio and print activities on behalf of the Japanese Association likely involve disseminating Japanese propaganda in the United States, such propaganda is not prohibited by law. He further explains that, after consulting with Mr. Ringwalt of the Far Eastern Division, it was decided that the formal departmental acknowledgment should be signed by an Assistant Secretary of State rather than a division chief.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Richard W. Flournoy to Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth regarding Brewer-Weeks Company

subfiles.about: Japanese Embassy submission of a list of 18 officials of the Naval Inspector's Office in New York requesting tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador submits Note No. 230 enclosing a roster of 18 naval officers, engineers, and clerks attached to the Naval Inspector's Office of the Imperial Japanese Navy Department in New York requesting income tax exemption on their official compensation. The Ambassador confirms all listed personnel are Japanese nationals whose duties consist of inspecting materials purchased by the government. Page 307 comprises the internal departmental transmittal cover addressed to Miss Marsh.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 230 transmitting list of Naval Inspector's Office personnel

subfiles.about: Secretary of State certification of reciprocity to Treasury for 18 Naval Inspector's Office personnel.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese Note No. 230 and the roster of 18 Naval Inspector's Office officials to Treasury Secretary Morgenthau, certifying reciprocal exemption under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936. Hull requests that the Treasury grant the exemption and advise the appropriate collectors of internal revenue.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: State Department acknowledgment of Japanese Note No. 230 regarding Naval Inspector's Office personnel.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 230 of November 20, 1937, enclosing the roster of 18 officials of the Naval Inspector's Office in New York, and notes that the request has been submitted to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Naval Inspector's Office personnel

subfiles.about: Japanese Embassy submission of a list of 20 officials of the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York requesting tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador transmits Note No. 229 and an attached list of 20 officials, engineers, and clerks attached to the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York seeking salary tax exemption. The note confirms all individuals are Japanese nationals whose duties involve inspecting purchased materials.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 229 transmitting list of Railway Office personnel

subfiles.about: Secretary of State certification of reciprocity to Treasury for 20 railway officials, highlighting expedited clearance for Masatoshi Nomura.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits Japanese Note No. 229 and the list of 20 railway officials to Secretary of the Treasury Morgenthau, certifying reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1936. Hull specifically requests expedited notice to the New York internal revenue collector regarding Masatoshi Nomura, who is scheduled to sail from New York on November 26.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury (Henry Morgenthau, Jr.)

subfiles.about: State Department acknowledgment of Japanese Note No. 229, noting expedited action requested for Masatoshi Nomura.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Note No. 229 and informs the Japanese Ambassador that the roster of 20 railway officials has been referred to the Treasury. The note confirms that, pursuant to the Embassy's informal request, expedited instructions were requested for Masatoshi Nomura ahead of his November 26 departure.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding Railway Office personnel and Masatoshi Nomura

subfiles.about: Treasury Department confirmation of income tax exemption for 20 railway officials and telegraphic clearance for Masatoshi Nomura.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury (Roswell Magill)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill advises Secretary of State Hull that the 20 officials attached to the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York are held exempt from Federal income tax. Magill confirms that the collector of internal revenue at the New York Customhouse was instructed by telegram on November 22 regarding Masatoshi Nomura's exempt status.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury Roswell Magill to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Department of State notification to the Japanese Ambassador confirming tax exemption for 20 railway officials.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State informs the Japanese Ambassador that the Treasury Department has ruled that the twenty officials attached to the Imperial Japanese Government Railway Office in New York City are exempt from Federal income tax on their official compensation. The note indicates that the collector of internal revenue in New York City is being advised accordingly.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note to the Japanese Ambassador regarding 20 Railway Office personnel
